title: Ganpati and Ketu
sub: Notes on this standalone talk by Brajesh Gautam, The Anchor Of Life: why Ganesh is worshipped first, the Ganesh birth story read as a lesson about doubt, Rahu and Ketu from the churning of the ocean, the astronomy behind Ganesh Chaturthi and eclipses, and prarabdha (fixed destiny).
desc: Complete notes on Ganpati and Ketu by Brajesh Gautam: why Ganesh comes first, the elephant-head birth story read as a lesson about doubt, Rahu and Ketu as shadow grahas, the astronomy behind Ganesh Chaturthi and solar or lunar eclipses, prarabdha, and household Ganesh placement rules, with video timestamps.
points: Doubt is the obstacle the whole myth is built around.
The Ganesh birth story, in his reading, punishes suspicion itself and replaces it with an elephant's calmer, larger mind.
Ganesh is worshipped before every other deity.
The speaker's claim is that any puja works better once doubt (Ganesh's domain) is cleared first.
Rahu and Ketu are shadow grahas, not simply evil.
Born from the churning of the ocean, Rahu drives raw ambition and Ketu is read as the cloud of doubt that can block it.
Ganesh Chaturthi has an astronomical basis in his account.
The Sun in Leo and the Moon in Pisces on the same day each year, read as a mouse-riding elephant.
Eclipses are read as a metaphor for destiny blocking clarity.
The moon passing between earth and sun mirrors, in his telling, prarabdha passing between a person and their own sense of direction.
Prarabdha has a ceiling the speaker calls fixed.
Accepting a blocked period is his suggested fix; fighting it only draws it out longer.
